note: Values were read out of the cited manufacturer documents on the retrieval date. Three cycle times in this file are SOURCE_DERIVED rather than published: the manufacturers publish a maximum throughput in labels or packs per minute, and 60 / that figure is seconds per label. The arithmetic is written into each value's basis, and every one of them is a BEST CASE under the conditions the manufacturer attaches to the maximum. They are not manufacturer cycle times and must never be shown as such.

candidates.product_scope: Labelling unit — mounted onto an existing conveyor or transfer system. The transport, the product sensor mounting and the frame are not part of this product.
candidates.description: Modular self-adhesive label applicator. Published labelling speed 0-30/50/80/150/200 m/min, label widths 80/160/240/320 mm, roll diameters 300/400/500/600 mm, supply 100-240 V AC 400 W, IP66, operating temperature 0-40 C, 4.3-inch colour touchscreen.

cycle_time_seconds.basis: HERMA publishes a maximum of 2,000 labels a minute; 60 / 2,000 = 0.03 s per label at that maximum.

caveats: The 200 m/min and 2,000 labels/min figures are published as maxima in synchronisation with the production line. The achievable rate depends on label length, label pitch and the transport, so the derived 0.03 s per label is a best case and not a station cycle time.
HERMA publishes no overall dimensions and no weight for the applicator on this page, so the installed envelope cannot be checked against the station's footprint from it.
No dispensing accuracy is published on this page.
The applicator dispenses onto a moving product; it does not transport the product itself.

candidates.product_scope: Complete print-and-apply labelling unit including printer, applicator and stand — the closest match in this file to a whole labelling station. The product transport is still separate.
candidates.description: Modular print-and-apply system. Published label sizes min. 12.5 x 7 mm to max. 160 x 210 mm, output up to 240 labels/min, print speed up to 400 mm/s, application stroke 50-1,200 mm depending on applicator, modes Tamp-Blow / Tamp-On / Wipe-On, supply 92-263 V 50-60 Hz 5 A, compressed air 6 bar per DIN ISO 8573-1.

cycle_time_seconds.basis: Weber publishes an output of up to 240 labels/min; 60 / 240 = 0.25 s per label at that maximum.

caveats: The 240 labels/min output is published as depending on label size, text change and dispense stroke, so the derived 0.25 s per label is a best case.
Weber publishes the weight as 75 kg 'depending on the version', and the 682 x 701 x 836 mm as the unit's own envelope — the swing of the application stroke needs clearance beyond it.
Label size is limited to 12.5 x 7 mm at minimum and 160 x 210 mm at maximum. A label outside that range needs a different applicator.
Requires compressed air at 6 bar (DIN ISO 8573-1). A station without an air supply cannot use this unit.
More than 1,500 applicator variants exist; the stroke, the mode and therefore the achievable rate depend on which one is configured.

candidates.category: Print-and-apply case labeller with pneumatic telescopic tamp
candidates.product_scope: Complete print-and-apply labelling unit, mounted beside a conveyor. The conveyor and the pack transport are not included.
candidates.description: Thermal transfer print-and-apply labeller with a pneumatic telescopic tamp and automatic pack detection. Published print speed 40-500 mm/sec, print resolution 300 dpi (200 dpi emulation), printheads 53/76/107 mm, label width 50-115 mm, label length 50-150 mm, roll capacity up to 400 mm spool, supply 90-260 V AC (115 W at 50 packs per minute), compressed air 6 bar, operating temperature 5-40 C.

cycle_time_seconds.basis: Videojet publishes a throughput of up to 60 packs per minute; 60 / 60 = 1.0 s per pack at that maximum.

interfaces: Configurable I/O (24 V, PNP and volt-free)
caveats: The 60 packs/min throughput is published as depending on label size and telescopic stroke, with a recommended maximum conveyor speed of 30 m/min. The derived 1.0 s per pack is therefore a best case.
Label size is limited to 50-115 mm wide and 50-150 mm long, dependent on the printhead version.
The 48 kg is published as a maximum excluding ribbon and labels.

Videojet gives the overall width and depth only as a dimensional drawing. The sheet states 820 mm height for the 160 mm model, which is a different variant from this one, so no envelope is recorded here and the footprint cannot be checked.
Requires compressed air at 6 bar, uncontaminated.
This is a case and pack labeller. Whether it suits a small electronics product is an engineering decision this concept does not yet specify.
